*Intermittent explosive disorder (IED) is characterized by episodes of loss of control over aggressive impulses, which can lead to verbal and/or physical aggression against people, animals, objects, oneself or other people and even other people's property. (IED) is part of the category of impulse control disorders, and anger outbursts have the characteristic of being impulsive and having no defined objective. In other words, none of the individual's actions are premeditated, he just has difficulty controlling his impulses. The aggressive reaction is always disproportionate to the situation, that is, the person becomes much more angry than would be considered appropriate in that situation. It's not about that explosive anger we feel when we see some injustice occurring, but rather about a person showing that same explosive anger for simply losing their car keys, for example. Even if the person is late or having a bad day, it is still not enough to explain the intensity of this reaction to such a common occurrence. In general, crises occur followed by a feeling of increasing tension, which reaches its peak and the person “explodes”. Afterwards, she feels relief instantly, and feelings of guilt, remorse, and shame often follow.*

The main symptoms of (IED) are:
*–Feelings of anger;*
*–Sensation of tension building up;*
*–Irritability;*
*–Quick thoughts;*
*–Tremors;*
*–Palpitations;*
*–Chest tightness;*
*–Feeling of having more energy;*
*–Screams;*
*–Getting into fights frequently;*
*–Trying to argue in situations where there is no need;*
*–Threatening others;*
*–Aggression against people or animals;*
*–Damaging property (own or someone else’s).*
